invalid.because: primitive is the singular "stat" rather than the registered primitive name, so a consumer dispatching on node.primitive would never match this block
primitive is missing altogether, leaving the class string as the only way to identify the node
the class string is missing the qe-dv-stats primitive token, so the renderer key div[class~=qe-dv-stats] never matches and the block renders as a bare table forever
the class string was not normalised: an author token duplicates a family token, which is exactly the work core's addClassOptions does not do for us
tone is outside the closed family vocabulary neutral | accent | good | warn | bad, so no consumer has a colour role for it
an item is missing the required display property, so a renderer would have to re-format value and lose the author's precision
an item carries a misspelt key (lable), which additionalProperties: false on the item must catch rather than read the item as label-less
an absent value carries the bespoke spelling "N/A" in display, when the family has exactly one: null in the properties, an em dash in the fallback
a scaled block leaves fraction null for a numeric value, so the mini bar silently never fills and nothing else flags it
denominator is zero, which is not a total anything can be measured against
three stats over two data rows: the props and the children disagree, which is the one defect the whole contract exists to prevent

invalid.because: the fallback table is ragged — the note column exists but the second data row has only two cells, and myst-to-typst emits cells as one flat positional sequence with no row delimiter, so every cell after the short row shifts one column left for the rest of the table
no item carries a note yet the fallback still emits a third column, so the table has a column the data does not have

a data row carries header: true, when only row 0 may: myst-to-tex writes an \hline after every row whose first cell is a header, and its long-table path then counts the whole table as running header and emits no body at all

row 0 holds the column names but no cell is marked header: true, so a plain theme renders them as ordinary <td> and myst-to-tex writes no \hline — the reader gets a table whose first row only looks like a header
only the first cell of the header row carries header: true, so the row is half a header: the HTML has one <th> among <td>s and the accessible column vocabulary is incomplete
a cell holds a card node, which myst-to-tex has no handler for: the whole subtree would be dropped from the PDF silently, with the build still exiting 0
contract is the number 1.0 rather than the string "1.0", so a version comparison would silently coerce and 1.10 would sort below 1.9
variant is outside the closed set headline | metric, so a renderer has no anatomy to choose
the fallback is a grid rather than a table: grid has no myst-to-tex handler, so the entire block would vanish from the PDF while the build exits 0
the fallback container is empty: an empty div with the data hidden in props does not implement this contract

the fallback table carries a label, an identifier and an html_id, so it is enumerated as "Table N", registered as a cross-reference target, and stripped of all three the moment the page is embedded elsewhere — the contract emits the table bare precisely so a stats block never steals a table number from the page it sits on

an item with no note renders a blank third cell instead of the em dash; the family has one spelling of an absent value — null in the properties, an em dash in the fallback — and no cell of a fallback table is ever blank, so the gap stays legible rather than reading as a rendering failure

the retired `naLabel` is carried on the root: the draft let each block spell a missing value for itself, contract 1.0 spells it one way — `null` in the properties, an em dash in the fallback — so a node still carrying the option sends a consumer looking for a string that means nothing
